statements.impact_statement: Netty SslHandler resource exhaustion vulnerability via SSLEngine. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious SSL/TLS data to a Netty server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run a TLS server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

statements.status_notes: An attacker can bypass IPv6 subnet rules due to an incorrect masking operation in IpSubnetFilterRule.compareTo(). Valid public IP addresses can bypass the restrictions. The io.netty.handler.ipfilter.IpSubnetFilterRule#compareTo(java.net.InetSocketAddress) method performs a bitwise AND between the incoming IP address and the configured networkAddress, instead of the subnetMask.
statements.impact_statement: Netty IpSubnetFilterRule IPv6 subnet filtering vulnerability fixed in 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed releases (pom.xml:116, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:308, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:73, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:60, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:51), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. The vulnerable access-control API is not reachable: a focused grep for IpSubnetFilterRule, io.netty.handler.ipfilter, RuleBasedIpFilter, UniqueIpFilter, and IpFilterRule across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: SslClientHelloHandler.decode() reads the 24-bit TLS handshake length and, when the ClientHello does not fit in the first record, eagerly allocates ctx.alloc().buffer(handshakeLength). Common SniHandler and AbstractSniHandler constructors can disable the length guard and timeout, allowing a 16 MiB request to cause immediate huge or unpooled allocation retained until the channel closes.
statements.impact_statement: Netty SslClientHelloHandler/SniHandler allocation vulnerability fixed in 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed releases (pom.xml:116, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:308, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:73, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:60, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:51), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. The vulnerable server-side SNI path is not reachable: a focused grep for SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, SslClientHelloHandler, netty.handler.ssl.Sni, ClientHello, SNIMatcher, and SNIHostName across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, SimpleTrustManagerFactory.engineGetTrustManagers() and related paths wrap any user-supplied plain X509TrustManager in X509TrustManagerWrapper, which extends X509ExtendedTrustManager but implements the 3-arg checkServerTrusted(chain, authType, SSLEngine) by discarding the SSLEngine and calling the 2-arg delegate. Because the object now IS an X509ExtendedTrustManager, neither SunJSSE's internal AbstractTrustManagerWrapper nor Netty's own OpenSslX509TrustManagerWrapper will re-wrap it to add endpoint-identification. Consequently, even though Netty 4.2 sets endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS" by default, a client built with `SslContextBuilder.forClient().trustManager(somePlainX509TrustManager)` performs no hostname verification at all. Versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final patch the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Netty hostname verification can be bypassed when client code passes a plain X509TrustManager through SslContextBuilder.forClient().trustManager(...). The scanner reported io.netty:netty-handler 4.1.133.Final, which is listed in the commercial distribution license metadata (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:526), but the source build now imports the patched Netty 4.1.135.Final BOM (pom.xml:114, pom.xml:116) and the liquibase-checks module imports the patched Netty 4.2.15.Final BOM (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:306, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:308). The vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase code: focused greps across Java sources for SslContextBuilder, SimpleTrustManagerFactory, trustManager(, and X509TrustManager returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.ssl.SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can cause an IndexOutOfBoundsException and invoke select(ctx, null). This selects the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific context. In deployments where per-SNI clientAuth=REQUIRE is the sole mutual TLS gate, the default SslContext uses clientAuth=NONE or clientAuth=OPTIONAL, and no application-layer certificate verification exists, an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the protected route's mutual TLS requirement. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException and fall back to the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific one. This only becomes an mTLS bypass in a deployment that (a) runs a Netty server accepting inbound TLS connections, (b) uses per-SNI SslContext selection as the sole mutual-TLS gate (clientAuth=REQUIRE on the SNI context, weaker on the default), and (c) has no application-layer certificate check. Liquibase never runs a Netty server: a grep across all Java sources for ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, and SslClientHelloHandler returns zero hits: netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the AWS SDK, the Couchbase client, the Cassandra JDBC driver). The scanner found netty-handler below the fixed versions in five bundled jars (Docker Scan run https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase-pro/actions/runs/34365994421): liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar 4.1.119.Final, liquibase-azure.jar 4.1.135.Final, liquibase-aws-extension.jar 4.1.136.Final, liquibase-commercial-couchbase.jar 4.2.16.Final, and liquibase-azure-deps.jar (unlabeled in the scan, same shaded copy as liquibase-azure.jar); none of them run a Netty server, so the version gap does not matter to this assessment.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, the default SniHandler constructors use pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation implemented in SslClientHelloHandler, which repeatedly recopies all previously received bytes each time it processes another fragment of a ClientHello split across TLS records. An unauthenticated attacker can advertise a large ClientHello and deliver it in thousands of tiny records, causing quadratic CPU consumption on the event loop and degrading TLS handling for other clients. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects the same pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation code in SslClientHelloHandler as CVE-2026-75595, already assessed in this file: a server-side SNI-routing feature that repeatedly recopies buffered bytes while reassembling a fragmented ClientHello, causing quadratic CPU consumption when an attacker splits a large ClientHello across many small TLS records. This only matters to a deployment running a Netty server with per-SNI SslContext selection (SniHandler/AbstractSniHandler). A source review found no references to ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, or SslClientHelloHandler anywhere in this repository; netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), none of which run a Netty server. The AWS extension already resolves netty-handler at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on 4.1.135.Final, the Cassandra extension on 4.1.130.Final, and the Couchbase client's shaded copy on 4.2.16.Final, all relying solely on the reachability argument.
